newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Greek consul bodyguard killed in south Albania.
newsitem.headline: Greek consul bodyguard killed in south Albania.

text.p: The bodyguard of the Greek consul in a troubled southern Albanian town was shot dead on Tuesday, the second foreign victim of the country's near-anarchy, local police and witnesses said.

Some witnesses said the killing of the bodyguard, named as Niko Markakis, may have been the work of a sniper although local police could not confirm this. He was inside the consulate building when a single shot rang out.
"The bodyguard of the consul was killed. We cannot say how this was done but the bullet hit him in the forehead," criminal police chief Agron Bere said in the town of Gjirokaster.
A police cordon was immediately thrown around the consulate, which has already been closed twice due to continuing unrest.
Gjirokaster was one of the areas hit by rebellion in February and March when public fury erupted over the collapse of crooked pyramid investment schemes.
Another Greek man was murdered in Albania's southern port of Vlore last week.
Markakis was shot as around five hundred Albanians were waiting for visas to Greece. Gjirokaster is a key transit point for Albanians wishing to enter Greece.
Violence continues to flare throughout Albania with the state exercises little or no authority in several regions.
Around a million weapons, ranging from grenades from rocket-launchers, were looted by people during February-March rioting.
